comment: cowdiff states for f_103162e8 (cow_seh_unwind_and_clear_record). The unit reads the SEH chain head from the harness TEB (@teb+0 - fs_base is the TEB, gthread.c:131 - this pin region was added for this unit), saves it, calls RtlUnwind(TargetFrame=[ebp+8], TargetIp=0x10316310, ExceptionRecord=[ebp+0xc], 0), and its finally clears EH_UNWINDING (bit 1) from the record's ExceptionFlags word while leaving every other bit and byte alone, then re-threads the chain: live head into the saved frame's link word, saved head back into fs:[0], live head returned in eax. The unwinder is the runtime's own shim (k32_misc.c), which ORs EH_UNWINDING (and EH_EXIT_UNWIND when TargetFrame is NULL) into [rec+4] and calls the handlers at [frame+4], so no --stub is needed: with the record always non-NULL the shim allocates nothing and is deterministic. Handler addresses are 0x100dc1f0, a converted function that only reads winmm's tick. STATE 2 IS THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS: the entry writes [F1+0] and fs:[0] with values the SHIM never touched (F2 was never anywhere near the head), so dropping either store is a real memory difference, not a same-value no-op. The @teb pin survives the per-state snapshot because the TEB page is now a tracked region. State 1: loop not entered (head == TargetFrame) - the record 0x11000008 -> shim 0x1100000A -> finally 0x11000008 proves both the set and the clear, and the upper byte 0x11 proves the dword is written back whole. State 3: TargetFrame NULL makes the shim OR EH_EXIT_UNWIND too; the record must end at 0x1100000c - a mask of 0xfb (clearing bit 2) fails there. State 4: loop stops on the sentinel after one unlink; eax is the live head.

states.note: head == TargetFrame: unwinder loop never runs; record 0x11000008 -> shim 0x1100000A -> finally 0x11000008; eax = frame 0x00981100; [0x00981100] = 0x00981100 and fs:[0] = 0x00981100

head F1 0x00981100, TargetFrame F1 itself so the shim never unlinks or calls a handler, and F1's link word starts at the 0xfeedf00d poison: the ENTRY alone must re-thread [F1+0] = live head F1 and fs:[0] = F1 - neither value was ever written by the shim, so deleting either store is a caught memory difference

TargetFrame NULL: the shim ORs EH_EXIT_UNWIND as well, so the record reaches 0x1100000E and the finally must leave 0x1100000C - bit 2 survives the 0xfd mask (bit 1 does not); chain stays the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel

loop ends on the sentinel after one unlink: head F1, F1 -> sentinel, TargetFrame F2 (never reached); the shim calls F1 handler (winmm tick thunk 0x100dbe00, stubbed to 5 so both sides answer the same) and fs:[0] becomes 0xFFFFFFFF; the finally re-links [F1]=0xFFFFFFFF, installs F1 into fs:[0], and eax = 0xFFFFFFFF (the LIVE head read before the install, not the saved one)
